Here we are, one more ticket for a question that has a one-line answer.

Introduction

Every infrastructure person knows the scene. You need to know if a colleague is in a group, or who is in a group, or in which OU an account lives. You have no access to the domain controller, no AD console, no RSAT. So you open a ticket, wait for someone to read it, and get back a screenshot two days later.

item.title: Kubernetes VPN Strongswan — IPsec with LDAP Auth
item.author: Lorenzo Girardi
item.description:
How to Manage VPN in a Kubernetes Environment

Traditional IPsec-XAuth VPN manages credentials in flat files. Adding a user means editing a file and redeploying. Removing a user means the same. In a Kubernetes environment, that’s not acceptable.

This implementation integrates Strongswan with LDAP, turning VPN access into a standard directory operation — the same system that manages every other credential in the organization.
